proxy_used.description: Peer-average trading P/B multiple applied to Family Bank's own book value per share
proxy_used.rationale: Family Bank listed on the NSE only on 2026-06-23 (by introduction, ~5.5 weeks before the reference date) after trading OTC since 2006. No sell-side analyst target price, rating, or coverage count could be found for FMLY as of the reference date, which is expected for a stock this newly listed. As a proxy for what the market currently implies, we applied the simple average of the trading P/B multiples of 9 NSE-listed peer banks already present in valuation_inputs.json's peer_banks block (Absa 1.69x, Co-op Bank 1.18x, DTB 0.36x, Equity Group 0.96x, I&M Group 0.64x, KCB Group 0.73x, NCBA 1.20x, Stanbic Holdings 1.44x, StanChart 1.81x; average = 1.112x) to Family Bank's own book value per share of KES 19.31098754702569 (from valuation_inputs.json company_facts.book_value_per_share, not independently re-derived). This gives an implied peer-multiple value of approximately KES 21.48, distinct from the actual traded price of KES 31.45.

notes: This is not a backtest (reference date 2026-08-02 equals the current date). Family Bank Limited listed on the NSE by introduction on 2026-06-23 at KES 18.00/share after decades of OTC trading; the stock has since been highly volatile (52-week range KES 18.00-50.00 per myStocks) and thinly seasoned, consistent with a fresh listing. No analyst consensus target price or rating was found in web search as of the reference date — coverage has not yet developed for this name. The actual traded price (KES 31.45, implying a market P/B of ~1.63x on book value per share of KES 19.31) sits well above the peer-average P/B proxy (~1.11x, implying ~KES 21.48), suggesting the market may currently be pricing in a listing-related scarcity/liquidity premium and/or growth optimism not yet reflected in peer multiples; a later report-writing stage should treat the peer-multiple proxy as a conservative anchor rather than a market consensus, and should flag the gap between traded price and peer-implied value explicitly rather than treating them as reconcilable.
